newsitem.title: USA: Hoechst sees commercial Topas in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst sees commercial Topas in 1997.

text.p: Hoechst AG expects to commercialize Topas, its cyclic olefin copolymer, in 1997, COC Project Manager Horst T. Land said Thursday.

In a Hoechst Research and Development Day presentation, he said the company sees a $200 million per year potential market for Topas, one of a new class of plastics manufactured by metallocene catalysts.
Land said the product, which Hoechst's Corporate Research & Technology unit has been working on since 1990, will compete with glass in many uses and with polycarbonates in compact discs.
Topas development has been a joint effort with Mitsui Petrochemical Industries Ltd since 1993, Land said.

Asked about competition from products planned by joint ventures formed by British Petroleum Co Plc and Dow Chemical Co, and Union Carbide Corp and Akzo Nobel NV, he said the products are not competitve.
